html:
Two Berber religious movements that ruled the Maghreb and Muslim Spain one after the other, from about 1040 to 1269. Both began as calls to purify Islam and both built empires from their base at Marrakesh.

The Almoravids came from the Sanhaja Berbers of the western Sahara. Around 1040 the preacher Abdallah ibn Yasin rallied them to a strict form of Maliki Sunni Islam. Their leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin founded Marrakesh around 1070 and took most of Morocco. When Christian Castile took Toledo in 1085, the Muslim kings of al-Andalus asked for his help. He beat Alfonso VI in 1086, then removed those kings and ruled Spain himself. Their gold dinars, made from trans-Saharan gold, were trusted across the Mediterranean.

The Almohads began with Ibn Tumart, a scholar of the Masmuda Berbers of the Atlas mountains, whose followers hailed him as the Mahdi around 1121. He preached God's absolute oneness and attacked the Almoravids as lax. His successor Abd al-Mumin took Marrakesh in 1147, then the whole Maghreb as far as Tunisia, and called himself caliph.

Almohad courts patronised the philosopher Averroes, yet the regime pressed Jews and Christians to convert; the family of Maimonides left Spain for this reason. Their great towers, like the Giralda of Seville, still stand.

A Christian coalition crushed the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212. Spain was soon lost, and the Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269.
sum: Two Berber religious movements that ruled the Maghreb and Muslim Spain one after the other, from about 1040 to 1269. Both began as calls to purify Islam and both built empires from their base at Marrakesh.
